lead: Antepartum haemorrhage is bleeding from the genital tract from 24 wk (28 wk in local definitions) until the end of the second stage; about 3–5% of pregnancies. The main causes are placenta praevia and abruption; vasa praevia and uterine rupture are rare but deadly.
f: Causes and assessment

Placental: praevia, abruption, marginal sinus bleed · Non-placental: vasa praevia, uterine rupture, show, cervical polyp or cancer · Unexplained: still raises preterm birth, FGR, stillbirth · History: amount, colour, pain, trigger, movements, previous CS · No digital PV until a scan excludes praevia; speculum then safe
Investigations and first hour

FBC, cross-match 4 units, clotting, fibrinogen, clot test (no clot in 7–10 min = low fibrinogen), creatinine, Kleihauer · CTG; ultrasound for placental site · Help, O₂, two cannulae, fluids, blood; O-negative if collapsed · Anti-D 500 IU within 72 h if RhD-negative + Kleihauer (1500 IU if none) · Peripheral unit: cannula, fluids, O₂, left tilt, transfer with a sample

sc: RhD-negative woman with APH at 32 wk → Anti-D 500 IU within 72 h + Kleihauer

f: Praevia versus abruption

Praevia: painless, bright red, recurrent; soft non-tender uterus; shock matches the loss; high head or malpresentation; diagnosis by ultrasound · Abruption: constant pain, dark blood or none; hard woody uterus; shock out of proportion; fetal distress; diagnosis is clinical

sc: Painless bleed, soft uterus, breech → Placenta praevia

f: Placenta praevia

Placenta in the lower segment · RCOG terms: low-lying (edge under 20 mm from the os) and praevia (covers the os); older grading minor/major · Low at 20 wk → rescan at 32 wk (most move up) · Risks: previous CS, previous praevia, multiparity, age over 35, smoking, twins, IVF · Bleeds because the stretching lower segment shears the placenta; thin muscle has no living ligature · TVS is safe (probe in the fornix); previous CS: Doppler ± MRI for accreta

tr: A transvaginal scan is safe in praevia; the danger is a finger in the cervix

f: Praevia: management

Heavy bleeding, unstable: resuscitate, caesarean at any gestation · Bleed settles, preterm: admit, steroids under 34 wk, blood ready · No bleeding: elective CS at 36–37 wk (RCOG 2018; local 37–38 wk) · Edge more than 2 cm from the os: vaginal birth can be tried · Bed bleeding at CS: oxytocin → sutures → balloon → artery ligation → hysterectomy

sc: G3, 34 wk, painless bright bleed, head high → Ultrasound for the placental site; no PV exam

f: Abruption

Premature separation of a normally sited placenta · Concealed or revealed · Risks: previous abruption, pre-eclampsia, trauma, smoking, cocaine, polyhydramnios with sudden ROM, thrombophilia · Clot strips the placenta → fetal hypoxia · Blood into the muscle → Couvelaire uterus · Thromboplastin → DIC (commonest cause of DIC in pregnancy) · Scan misses most clots · Complications: shock, DIC, PPH, AKI, Sheehan, fetal death

tr: Couvelaire uterus is not itself a reason for hysterectomy: uterotonics, massage, compression sutures first

f: Abruption: management

Mother unstable or DIC: resuscitate, correct clotting (tranexamic acid 1 g IV, platelets if under 50, FFP 15 mL/kg), deliver now; no IM injections · Fetus alive and distressed: emergency caesarean · Fetus dead, mother stable: vaginal birth, ARM + oxytocin (labour is fast)

sc: Abruption, FHR absent, mother stable → ARM + oxytocin, vaginal birth
Bleeding from cannula sites → DIC: FFP, cryoprecipitate

f: Placenta accreta spectrum

Deficient decidua; villi attach too deep · Accreta on the myometrium (about 75%), increta into it, percreta through the serosa into bladder or bowel · Risk with praevia + previous CS: none 3%, one 11%, two 40%, three or more 60% · Usually silent; percreta may cause haematuria · Colour Doppler in every praevia with a scar; MRI if unclear · Scan signs: lost clear zone, lacunae, thin myometrium, bridging vessels · Plan at a specialist centre, consent for hysterectomy, 6–8 units, CS at about 36 wk, incision away from the placenta · Do not pull the placenta: hysterectomy with it in place

sc: Anterior praevia with 2 previous CS → Colour Doppler ± MRI for accreta

f: Vasa praevia

Fetal vessels in the membranes over the os; they tear at ROM: the blood lost is fetal · Types: velamentous insertion; vessels between lobes (bilobed, succenturiate) · Undiagnosed: about 60% of babies die; a term baby has only 250–300 mL of blood · Triad: ROM + painless small bleed + fetal distress (bradycardia or sinusoidal CTG); mother well · Known before labour: admit 30–32 wk, CS at 34–36 wk before ROM · Bleeding in labour: immediate CS; fully dilated with the head low: instrumental · Apt test or Kleihauer, but never wait

sc: Bleed at ROM, FHR 80, fully dilated, head at +2 → Instrumental delivery now

f: Uterine rupture

Complete (all layers) or incomplete (dehiscence, serosa intact) · Risks: scar (about 0.5% after one lower-segment CS, 4–9% after a classical scar), obstructed labour in a multipara, oxytocin or misoprostol overdose, grand multiparity · Impending: Bandl's ring rising, tender lower segment, tachycardia, haematuria · Rupture: pain, contractions stop, presenting part rises, fetal parts under the skin, fetal bradycardia, shock · Resuscitate, laparotomy: repair a clean tear or hysterectomy; check the bladder · Prevent: partograph, no oxytocin in obstruction, VBAC only in hospital

sc: VBAC in labour: sudden pain, contractions stop, FHR 70 → Resuscitate, immediate laparotomy
tr: Obstructed labour in a primigravida → fistula more likely; in a multipara → rupture more likely
